Obama is a [Protestant](/wiki/Protestant "Protestant") Christian whose religious views developed in his adult life.[[108]](#cite_note-Christian-109) He wrote in *[The Audacity of Hope](/wiki/The_Audacity_of_Hope "The Audacity of Hope")* that he "was not raised in a religious household." He described his mother, raised by non-religious parents, as being detached from religion, yet "in many ways the most spiritually awakened person ... I have ever known", and "a lonely witness for [secular humanism](/wiki/Secular_humanism "Secular humanism")." He described his father as a "confirmed [atheist](/wiki/Atheist "Atheist")" by the time his parents met, and his stepfather as "a man who saw religion as not particularly useful." Obama explained how, through working with [black churches](/wiki/Black_church "Black church") as a [community organizer](/wiki/Community_organizer "Community organizer") while in his twenties, he came to understand "the power of the African-American religious tradition to spur social change."[[109]](#cite_note-social_change-110)

Jiang Zemin :: part 05 :: chunk_0004
Jiang came to power unexpectedly as a compromise candidate following the [1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre](/wiki/1989_Tiananmen_Square_protests_and_massacre "1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre"), when he replaced [Zhao Ziyang](/wiki/Zhao_Ziyang "Zhao Ziyang") as CCP general secretary after Zhao was ousted for his support for the student movement. Jiang also assumed the chairmanship of the Central Military Commission from Deng Xiaoping. As the involvement of the [Eight Elders](/wiki/Eight_Elders "Eight Elders") in Chinese politics steadily declined, Jiang consolidated his hold on power to become the "paramount leader" and "core leader" in 1989.[[b]](#cite_note-2) Urged by [Deng Xiaoping's southern tour](/wiki/Deng_Xiaoping%27s_southern_tour "Deng Xiaoping's southern tour") in 1992, Jiang officially introduced the term [socialist market economy](/wiki/Socialist_market_economy "Socialist market economy") in his speech during the [14th CCP National Congress](/wiki/14th_National_Congress_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "14th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party") held later that year, which accelerated [reform and opening up](/wiki/Reform_and_opening_up "Reform and opening up"). In the economy, Jiang's administration oversaw the breaking of the [iron rice bowl](/wiki/Iron_rice_bowl "Iron rice bowl"), started several key infrastructure projects and privatized many [state-owned enterprises](/wiki/State-owned_enterprises_of_China "State-owned enterprises of China"). Earvin Johnson Jr. was born in [Lansing, Michigan](/wiki/Lansing,_Michigan "Lansing, Michigan"), to [General Motors](/wiki/General_Motors "General Motors") assembly worker Earvin Sr. and school janitor Christine.[[23]](#cite_note-23) Johnson, who had six siblings and three half-siblings by his father's previous marriage,[[24]](#cite_note-24)[[25]](#cite_note-mylife-25)[[a]](#cite_note-27) was influenced by his parents' strong work ethic. His mother spent many hours after work each night cleaning their home and preparing the next day's meals, while his father did janitorial work at a used car lot and collected garbage, all while never missing a day at General Motors. Johnson would often help his father on the garbage route, and he was teased by neighborhood children who called him "Garbage Man".[[27]](#cite_note-siblings-28) His mother raised him in the [Seventh-day Adventist Church](/wiki/Seventh-day_Adventist_Church "Seventh-day Adventist Church").[[28]](#cite_note-29)[[29]](#cite_note-30)

Johnson came to love basketball as a young man. His favorite basketball player growing up was [Bill Russell](/wiki/Bill_Russell "Bill Russell"), whom he admired more for his many championships than his athletic ability.[[30]](#cite_note-bill-31) He also idolized players such as [Earl Monroe](/wiki/Earl_Monroe "Earl Monroe") and [Marques Haynes](/wiki/Marques_Haynes "Marques Haynes"),[[31]](#cite_note-32) and practiced "all day".[[32]](#cite_note-nbafullbio-33) Johnson came from an athletic family. His father played high school basketball in his home state of Mississippi,[[33]](#cite_note-senior-34) and Johnson learned the finer points about the game from him. Johnson's mother, originally from [North Carolina](/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina"),[[33]](#cite_note-senior-34) had also played basketball as a child, and she grew up watching her brothers play the game.[[30]](#cite_note-bill-31)

[1G](/wiki/1G "1G") [TACS](/wiki/TACS "TACS") networks were provided by China Telecom since 1987, operations transferred to China Mobile in 1999, the year China Mobile established, 1G shut down in 2001.

To call phone numbers in China one of the following formats is used:

* For fixed phones:

**xxx xxxx** | **xxxx xxxx** Calls within the same area code

**0yyy xxx xxxx** | **0yyy xxxx xxxx** Calls from other areas within China

**+86 yyy xxx xxxx** | **+86 yyy xxxx xxxx** Calls from outside China

* For mobile phones:

**1nn xxxx xxxx** Calls to mobile phones within China

**+86 1nn xxxx xxxx** Calls to mobiles from outside China

The prefix one is used exclusively by the national capital, [Beijing](/wiki/Beijing "Beijing") [Municipality](/wiki/Direct-controlled_municipalities_of_China "Direct-controlled municipalities of China").

* [Beijing](/wiki/Beijing "Beijing") – 10 (formerly 1, abolished after GSM was introduced, to avoid conflict with mobile phone numbers with prefix 0 added (e.g. 0139-xxxx-xxxx))
